title: The Fatigue of High Standards When Selecting Talent
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article names a specific failure mode in hiring: 'selection fatigue,' where a team that starts with rigorous standards gradually wears down after rejecting candidate after candidate, and ends up settling for a weaker hire than ones passed over earlier. Rather than recommending teams simply push through with willpower, it argues for applying systems thinking — when a process repeatedly fails to produce a good outcome, the fix is to change an element of the system itself, not repeat the same steps hoping for a different result. It offers concrete examples: switching talent sources, recomposing the interview panel, adding new diagnostics, or requiring a skills demonstration. The piece frames this as a way to break the logjam without compromising the standards that matter for long-term team quality.
points: 'Selection fatigue' causes teams to settle for weaker hires as the rejection pile grows.
Ironically, the eventual 'settled for' candidate is often weaker than ones rejected earlier in the process.
The recommended fix is systems thinking: change an element of the process, not lower the bar.
Concrete system changes include new talent sources, a different interview panel, or added diagnostics.
The goal is preserving high standards for talent while breaking the logjam that fatigue creates.
quotes: Leaders who reject inferior answers or solutions until the team finds a better one can wear people down.
The temptation to accept a workable decision becomes ever stronger as time marches on.
Somewhat ironically, the talent choice made after selection fatigue has worn down the team ends up being more than a compromise.
Any time a system consistently fails to produce the desired outcome, the answer is not to repeat the same process but to change the system.
Great leaders don’t lower their standards for talent nor submit to selection fatigue.
